Taiwan is known for its railroad network. If people want to travel comfortably around Taiwan, trains are the most common [[1]] that most tourists would choose. A train trip can take more than eight hours, and the meal of choice for many riders on board is the train “bento,” or what some would call “lunch-box,” provided on the train or at station kiosks. Taiwan Railways Administration can sell up to 10 million train bentos every year, not yet [[2]] those sold at convenience stores and nearby restaurants.
Train bentos in Taiwan [[3]] from Japan. The first train bento, sold in Japan in 1885, was takeaway rice balls. Taiwan was governed by Japan between 1895 and 1945, and it was during this [[4]] period that this meal made its way into Taiwan. During the early years after the rule of Japan, train travel in Taiwan was a big event that most children would eagerly [[5]] because it was something that took place only on special occasions. For many Taiwanese people who grew up in the 1950s and 1960s, the flavors of train bentos was thus [[6]] with memories of holiday travels or family gatherings. This may partly explain train bento’s lasting popularity in Taiwan.
Over time, the flavors of train bentos get [[7]] as well. A typical train bento in Taiwan boasts a slice of pickles, a mouthful of fatty Taiwanese sausage, an egg cooked with traditional soy sauce, and a braised pork cutlet as big as one’s hand. The train bentos in Taiwan nowadays have been very different from the original [[8]] sold in Japan.
In some train stations, the box of train bentos is the attraction itself. One such location is Chishang, a village in Taitung that is famous for rice. Chishang train bento takes advantage of the local rice to make the meal and is sold in wooden boxes, which is regarded by many as its [[9]] trait. Another popular bento station is Fenchihu, the central stop along the railway to Alishan. The restaurant there serves train bentos in a metal tin that must be returned, and souvenir tins are [[10]] for purchase at the same time. For some tourists, the peculiar outlook of train bentos seems to outweigh the food inside.
